why: A small state machine over an array: keep the memory array plus a map from allocation id to (start, length), and apply each query exactly as described, including the rules for failed allocations and unknown ids.
hints: What state has to survive between queries?
The memory array, the next allocation id, and id -> (start, length) for live allocations. Initially occupied units belong to no id.

Allocate: scan left to right for the first run of x zeros, mark it, record it, output start and bump the id. Erase: pop the id if present, zero its units, output its length. O(n) per query is fine at 2000 x 2000.
pitfalls: A failed allocation outputs -1 and does not consume an id.
Erasing an id twice, or one that never existed, outputs -1.
When a run is broken by a 1, reset the run length to 0.
